domain_label: Known/Unknown Mapping & Uncertainty Taxonomy (Knowledge Acquisition subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the stance is neutral and epistemic: the method types and maps uncertainty, it does not adjudicate the truth of domain claims
scope is bounded to a single question or decision within a session; cross-session knowledge management is delegated to sibling KBs
downstream evidence weighting and acquisition execution are consumers of this map, not part of it
exclusions: executing the acquisition itself (queries, experiments, elicitation runs) — delegated to the acquisition pipeline
domain-specific truth adjudication of any particular claim
long-horizon organizational knowledge management and archival
formal probability calculus and statistical estimation internals (assumed available as tools)
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for known/unknown mapping and uncertainty-taxonomy work units, informed by the Johari window, the risk/uncertainty distinction, the Walker et al. uncertainty taxonomy, and deep-uncertainty/robust-decision literature; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Luft & Ingham 1955 (Johari window); Knight 1921 Risk, Uncertainty and Profit (risk vs uncertainty); Walker, Harremoes, Rotmans, van der Sluijs, van Asselt, Janssen & Krayer von Krauss 2003 'Defining Uncertainty: A Conceptual Basis for Uncertainty Management in Model-Based Decision Support'; Lempert, Popper & Bankes 2003 (RAND) Shaping the Next One Hundred Years: robust decision making under deep uncertainty; Walker, Lempert & Kwakkel 2013 'Deep Uncertainty'; Taleb 2007 The Black Swan (unknown-unknowns, used with caution); Howard 1966 (value of information); Funtowicz & Ravetz 1990 (NUSAP / uncertainty in science)

competency_questions.question: How is a claim typed across the four knowledge cells (known-known, known-unknown, unknown-known, unknown-unknown), and what does each require?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KNOWN_KNOWN needs awareness plus justification, KNOWN_UNKNOWN is a named gap, UNKNOWN_KNOWN is surfaced tacit knowledge, UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN is bounded ignorance

competency_questions.question: How are decision-relevant knowledge gaps identified and deduplicated against existing knowns and pseudo-gaps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KNOWN_UNKNOWN names gaps; GAP_IDENTIFY enumerates and deduplicates them

competency_questions.question: How are unknown-knowns surfaced and how is the full ignorance taxonomy applied to each item?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNKNOWN_KNOWN elicits tacit knowledge; IGNORANCE_TYPING assigns each item a complete type

competency_questions.question: How are unknown-unknowns bounded and actively probed for to reduce false closure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN bounds the cell; DISCONFIRMATION actively probes to convert them into named gaps

competency_questions.question: How is uncertainty classified as aleatory versus epistemic, and why does the distinction change treatment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ALEATORY marks irreducible variability handled as a distribution; EPISTEMIC marks reducible-by-evidence uncertainty routed to acquisition

competency_questions.question: How is deep (Knightian) uncertainty distinguished from ordinary epistemic uncertainty and handled once recognized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEEP_UNCERTAINTY flags non-probabilistic uncertainty distinct from reducible EPISTEMIC and routes it to robustness/scenario methods

competency_questions.question: How are structural/model and measurement/parameter uncertainties separated and why does the order matter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODEL_UNC isolates framing/structure uncertainty; MEASUREMENT_UNC isolates input/parameter uncertainty, valid only within a validated structure

competency_questions.question: How is ambiguity/linguistic uncertainty detected and dissolved without costly empirical acquisition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AMBIGUITY_UNC resolves vague terms by definition rather than evidence before a gap is listed

competency_questions.question: How are assumptions recorded as conditional knowns so dependence on them is explicit and revisitable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSUMPTION_REGISTRY records assumptions as conditional knowns linked to dependent conclusions

competency_questions.question: How is confidence typed per claim, propagated through inferences, and gated for downstream use?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_STATE types confidence; UNC_PROPAGATION carries it honestly; CONFIDENCE_LEGALITY gates downstream use by label

competency_questions.question: What does a complete type for an item consist of, and how is the frontier between known and unknown rendered and kept current?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IGNORANCE_TYPING assigns cell+nature+recognition; BOUNDARY_OF_KNOWLEDGE renders the frontier and MAP_MAINTENANCE keeps it living

competency_questions.question: How are gaps prioritized for acquisition by value of information against cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GAP_IDENTIFY enumerates gaps and GAP_PRIORITIZE ranks them by decision-impact relative to acquisition cost and feasibility

competency_questions.question: How is an inaccessible target quantity approached via proxy/surrogate knowledge without being misled by drift?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROXY_KNOWN selects a correlated observable and records its bias and validity conditions

competency_questions.question: What rules govern whether a given confidence label may support a downstream claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_LEGALITY maps confidence labels and uncertainty types to permitted downstream uses

glossary.definition: a proposition the inquirer is aware of holding and can justify with evidence, usable without further acquisition
a gap the inquirer is consciously aware of and can name as an answerable question
tacit or implicit knowledge held but not made explicit, hence unavailable for audit
ignorance the inquirer is not aware of: questions not asked and failure modes not imagined
variability inherent in the phenomenon that more knowledge cannot reduce, only characterize as a distribution
uncertainty from lack of knowledge about a fixed quantity, reducible in principle by acquiring evidence
a situation where the probability distribution or even the outcome set is unknown or contested, requiring robustness not optimization
the expected improvement in a decision from resolving a particular uncertainty, net of acquisition cost
an assumption treated as true-for-now and recorded with the conclusions that depend on it
a calibrated, evidence-labeled qualifier (with interval) attached to a claim and carried downstream
a correlated observable used to stand in for an inaccessible target quantity, recorded with its bias
the rendered boundary between populated knowledge cells and open or unrecognized regions

nodes.definition: Type a claim as a known-known: a proposition the inquirer is aware of holding AND can justify with cited evidence, so it can be used directly without further acquisition.

base.update_signal: justification standard or evidence threshold for 'known' changes

included: awareness + justification test for a claim
excluded: measuring how reducible the residual uncertainty is

pros.claim: A justified known-known is the only cell whose content may be consumed without acquisition, so typing it cleanly prevents wasted re-research
pros.example: 'service SLA is 99.9%' cited from the signed contract is usable now

cons.claim: Overclaiming known-known status converts an assumption into a false certainty that propagates silently
cons.example: treating a vendor's marketing number as a justified known

failure_modes: unjustified belief mislabeled known-known
stale known not re-checked against new evidence
acceptance_tests: each known-known carries an explicit justification and evidence reference
revisit_triggers: justification standard revised
a known-known is contradicted by new evidence

nodes.definition: Type a question as a known-unknown: a gap the inquirer is consciously aware of and can name, making it an addressable target for acquisition or estimation.

base.update_signal: the catalog of named open questions changes

included: naming a gap as an explicit question
attaching an acquisition or estimation handle

pros.claim: A named known-unknown is the unit acquisition can act on: you can plan a query, an experiment, or an elicitation for it
pros.example: 'we don't know peak QPS' becomes a load-test task

cons.claim: A growing list of known-unknowns can create an illusion of completeness that hides the unknown-unknowns beyond it
cons.example: an exhaustive risk register that still misses the novel failure

failure_modes: gap stated too vaguely to be acquirable
known-unknown left without an acquisition handle
acceptance_tests: every known-unknown is phrased as an answerable question with an acquisition or estimation route
revisit_triggers: new open question surfaced
a known-unknown is resolved or reframed

nodes.definition: Type and surface unknown-knowns: knowledge the inquirer or team implicitly holds (tacit skill, embedded assumption, institutional memory) but has not made explicit, so it is unavailable for justification or audit.

base.update_signal: elicitation method or tacit-knowledge inventory changes

included: eliciting implicit/tacit knowledge into explicit claims

pros.claim: Surfacing an unknown-known converts hidden tacit knowledge into an auditable, sharable known-known and removes a class of silent assumptions
pros.example: an engineer's unstated 'the cache is always warm' written down and tested

cons.claim: Aggressive elicitation can over-formalize tacit skill that resists articulation, producing brittle or false explicit rules
cons.example: forcing a heuristic feel into a rigid checklist that breaks on edge cases

failure_modes: tacit assumption never surfaced and silently relied upon
elicited tacit rule mis-states the actual skill
acceptance_tests: material tacit assumptions are elicited into explicit, testable claims
revisit_triggers: new participant or system brings unsurfaced tacit knowledge
an elicited rule is found to misrepresent practice

nodes.definition: Type and bound unknown-unknowns: ignorance the inquirer is not even aware of (questions not asked, failure modes not imagined), which cannot be listed directly and must be probed for indirectly.

base.update_signal: a previously unimagined failure or question class is discovered

included: bounding the space of unimagined questions

pros.claim: Naming the unknown-unknown cell, even though its contents cannot be listed, licenses humility margins and active probing instead of false closure
pros.example: reserving a 'surprise budget' rather than claiming the risk list is complete

cons.claim: Unbounded fear of unknown-unknowns can paralyze decision-making or justify infinite search
cons.example: refusing to ship until every conceivable surprise is ruled out

failure_modes: false closure: treating the known map as the whole territory
unbounded search chasing hypothetical surprises
acceptance_tests: the map records an explicit residual-ignorance margin and at least one active probe for unknown-unknowns
revisit_triggers: a realized surprise reveals a missed question class
scope or environment changes materially

nodes.definition: Classify uncertainty as aleatory: variability inherent in the phenomenon (stochastic, chance-driven) that more knowledge about the system cannot reduce, only characterize as a distribution.

base.update_signal: the system boundary that fixes what counts as inherent variability changes

pros.claim: Tagging uncertainty aleatory tells acquisition to stop seeking facts and instead estimate a distribution, saving wasted reduction effort
pros.example: dice-roll variability is modeled, not 'researched away'

cons.claim: The aleatory/epistemic split is model-relative: what looks irreducible may be epistemic under a finer model, so a hard label can entrench avoidable ignorance
cons.example: calling weather 'random' when a better model would reduce it

failure_modes: epistemic gap mislabeled aleatory (gives up reducible knowledge)
aleatory variability quantified with a spuriously tight distribution
acceptance_tests: each aleatory tag states the system boundary under which the variability is treated as irreducible
revisit_triggers: system boundary or model resolution changes
apparent variability is reduced by a new model

nodes.definition: Classify uncertainty as epistemic: it stems from lack of knowledge about a fixed-but-unknown quantity and can in principle be reduced by acquiring evidence, marking it a candidate for the gap pipeline.

base.update_signal: new evidence channels make a previously irreducible quantity reducible

pros.claim: Marking uncertainty epistemic identifies exactly where acquisition can buy down uncertainty, so value-of-information analysis applies
pros.example: an unknown constant becomes a measurable target

cons.claim: Treating deep or aleatory uncertainty as merely epistemic breeds overconfidence: it promises reduction that evidence cannot actually deliver
cons.example: a 'just measure it' stance toward a genuinely deep uncertainty

failure_modes: aleatory or deep uncertainty mislabeled epistemic
epistemic reduction assumed cheaper than it is
acceptance_tests: each epistemic tag names a concrete evidence channel that could reduce it
revisit_triggers: a reduction effort fails to move the uncertainty
the quantity is reclassified as aleatory or deep

nodes.definition: Identify model/structural uncertainty (Walker et al.): uncertainty about the form of the model or framing itself — wrong variables, wrong relationships, wrong boundaries — distinct from uncertainty in its inputs.

base.update_signal: the modeling framework or its scenario set is revised

pros.claim: Separating structural from parametric uncertainty prevents the classic error of tuning parameters of a wrong model and calling it reduced
pros.example: exploring rival causal structures rather than refitting one

cons.claim: Structural uncertainty resists quantification: enumerating alternative model forms is open-ended and can shade into deep uncertainty
cons.example: you cannot list all wrong framings of a novel system

failure_modes: parameter tuning masquerades as structural validation
alternative model forms never enumerated
acceptance_tests: at least one rival model structure or framing is articulated and compared
revisit_triggers: model framework changes
a rival structure better explains the data

nodes.definition: Identify measurement/parameter uncertainty (Walker et al.): uncertainty in the values of inputs and parameters given a fixed model structure — sampling error, instrument error, estimate spread.

base.update_signal: measurement instrument, sampling design, or parameter source changes

pros.claim: Parameter uncertainty is the most tractable kind: it has well-developed estimation and interval methods, so it can often be reduced cheaply
pros.example: a confidence interval on a measured rate from more samples

cons.claim: Reducing parameter uncertainty within a wrong model gives false precision about the wrong thing
cons.example: tighter intervals on a parameter of a misspecified model

failure_modes: parameter precision reported without model-validity caveat
sampling bias treated as random error
acceptance_tests: each measurement-uncertainty estimate states its source (sampling/instrument) and an interval, not a point
revisit_triggers: instrument or sampling design changes
a parameter estimate is revised by new data

nodes.definition: Identify ambiguity/linguistic uncertainty: imprecision arising from the question or terms themselves — vagueness, context-dependence, underspecification — which is dissolved by definition, not by evidence.

base.update_signal: term definitions or the question framing change

pros.claim: Catching ambiguity first prevents pseudo-gaps: an 'unknown' that is really an undefined term is dissolved by definition, not costly acquisition
pros.example: 'is it fast?' resolved by defining a latency target, not by measurement

cons.claim: Over-operationalizing can prematurely narrow a genuinely open concept and discard relevant meanings
cons.example: pinning 'quality' to one metric and losing the rest

failure_modes: ambiguity mis-routed to empirical acquisition
operational definition silently narrows the question
acceptance_tests: each ambiguity-tagged item is resolved by an explicit definition or operationalization before acquisition is planned
revisit_triggers: term definitions revised
a defined term is found to mismatch stakeholder intent

nodes.definition: Identify deep (Knightian / level-4+) uncertainty: situations where parties cannot agree on the probability distribution or even the full set of outcomes, so standard probabilistic reduction does not apply and decisions need robustness, not optimization.

base.update_signal: the agreed outcome set or distribution becomes contested or unknown

excluded: well-characterized risk with an agreed distribution

pros.claim: Naming deep uncertainty honestly switches the method from optimizing a known distribution to seeking decisions robust across many futures (RAND/Lempert RDM)
pros.example: planning that performs acceptably across scenarios rather than betting on one forecast

cons.claim: Declaring deep uncertainty too readily abandons tractable estimation and can excuse analytical laziness
cons.example: calling a measurable quantity 'deeply uncertain' to avoid the work

failure_modes: deep uncertainty forced into a single point estimate (overconfidence)
tractable uncertainty abandoned as 'deep' to avoid analysis
acceptance_tests: deep-uncertainty items are handled by robustness/scenario analysis, not a single probability estimate
revisit_triggers: outcome set or distribution becomes contested
a robust option set is invalidated by a new scenario

nodes.definition: Maintain a registry of assumptions: unverified propositions the inquiry depends on, recorded as conditional knowns (true-for-now, pending check) with the conclusions that rest on each, so dependence is explicit and revisitable.

base.update_signal: an assumption is invalidated or a new load-bearing assumption is added

included: linking each assumption to dependent conclusions

pros.claim: Treating assumptions as flagged conditional knowns keeps inferences usable while making every dependence auditable and falsifiable
pros.example: tagging 'assume traffic doubles' so all sizing rests visibly on it

cons.claim: A bloated assumption registry can hide which assumptions are actually load-bearing for the decision
cons.example: hundreds of logged assumptions, none ranked by impact

failure_modes: load-bearing assumption left unrecorded
assumption recorded but not linked to what depends on it
acceptance_tests: every load-bearing assumption is registered as a conditional known with its dependent conclusions and a check route
revisit_triggers: an assumption is contradicted
a new conclusion adds a hidden dependence

nodes.definition: Attach a typed confidence state to each claim: a calibrated, evidence-labeled qualifier (e.g. justified / provisional / speculative with an interval) that travels with the claim for downstream use.

base.update_signal: the confidence vocabulary or calibration standard changes

included: attaching an evidence label and interval

pros.claim: A typed, calibrated confidence state lets downstream reasoning weight claims correctly instead of treating all knowns as equal
pros.example: a 'provisional, 0.4-0.7' tag stops a weak claim being used as a hard fact

cons.claim: Numeric confidence invites false precision — a fabricated 0.73 can look more authoritative than an honest 'roughly even'
cons.example: attaching three-decimal probabilities to subjective hunches

failure_modes: false precision in confidence numbers
confidence assigned without calibration or evidence basis
acceptance_tests: each claim carries a calibrated confidence state with an evidence label and an interval, not a bare point
revisit_triggers: calibration check fails
confidence vocabulary is revised

nodes.definition: Apply the full ignorance taxonomy to each item: assign its knowledge cell, its uncertainty nature (aleatory/epistemic/ambiguity/model/measurement/deep), and whether it is recognized — giving every item a complete type before it is acted on.

base.update_signal: the taxonomy categories or their decision rules change

included: assigning a complete type (cell + nature + recognition)

pros.claim: A complete type per item makes the right treatment derivable: define-vs-measure-vs-distribution-vs-robustness follows from the type
pros.example: ambiguity -> define; epistemic -> acquire; aleatory -> distribution; deep -> robustness

cons.claim: Forcing every item into one box ignores that real items are blends, and category boundaries are themselves uncertain
cons.example: an item that is part-ambiguous, part-empirical typed as only one

failure_modes: items left untyped and acted on by default
blended uncertainty forced into a single category
acceptance_tests: every mapped item carries a cell type, a nature type, and a recognition flag
revisit_triggers: taxonomy categories revised
an item's type is found to mislead its treatment

nodes.definition: Identify knowledge gaps: enumerate the known-unknowns and reducible-epistemic items that bear on the question, deduplicated against existing knowns and ambiguity-only pseudo-gaps.

base.update_signal: the question scope or the set of relevant gaps changes

pros.claim: A deduplicated gap list scoped to the decision keeps acquisition focused on what actually matters, not every conceivable unknown
pros.example: dropping a gap that, once defined, was already a known

cons.claim: Gap identification can never be provably exhaustive, so a complete-looking list can mask the unknown-unknowns beyond it
cons.example: a tidy gap list that omits the failure no one imagined

failure_modes: pseudo-gap (really ambiguity) listed as empirical gap
duplicate of an existing known listed as a gap
acceptance_tests: each identified gap is decision-relevant, distinct from existing knowns, and not merely an undefined term
revisit_triggers: question scope changes
a listed gap is found to duplicate a known or an ambiguity

nodes.definition: Prioritize identified gaps by value of information: rank each gap by how much resolving it would change the decision, weighed against the cost and feasibility of acquiring it, so scarce effort buys the most decision-relevance.

base.update_signal: the decision, its payoffs, or acquisition costs change

pros.claim: Value-of-information ranking stops the team from researching a low-impact unknown while a decision-flipping gap stays open
pros.example: prioritizing the gap that would change go/no-go over a cosmetic detail

cons.claim: VoI estimates depend on a decision model that may itself be wrong, so the ranking inherits that model's blind spots
cons.example: ranking under a payoff model that omits the real driver

failure_modes: effort spent on low-VoI gaps while high-VoI gaps stay open
VoI computed from a mis-specified decision model
acceptance_tests: gaps are ranked by decision-impact against acquisition cost, with the top gaps justified
revisit_triggers: the decision or its payoffs change
a resolved gap fails to move the decision as ranked

nodes.definition: Map the boundary of knowledge: render the frontier between what is known and what is not as an explicit artifact, marking which cells are populated, which gaps are open, and where the recognized map ends.

base.update_signal: the frontier shifts as knowns are added or gaps are opened

included: rendering the known/unknown frontier as an artifact
marking the edge of the recognized map
excluded: the active probing beyond the frontier

pros.claim: An explicit frontier artifact communicates at a glance what is settled, what is open, and where confidence ends, aligning a team's epistemic state
pros.example: a one-page map showing knowns, open gaps, and a 'here be dragons' margin

cons.claim: Any drawn boundary implies the far side is empty, subtly encouraging the false-closure error the map is meant to fight
cons.example: a crisp frontier read as 'nothing important beyond here'

failure_modes: frontier drawn as if it were the edge of all relevant truth
boundary not updated as knowledge shifts
acceptance_tests: the frontier artifact distinguishes populated cells, open gaps, and an explicit residual-ignorance margin
revisit_triggers: a known or gap changes the frontier
the boundary is treated as complete

nodes.definition: Establish proxy/surrogate knowledge for inaccessible facts: when a target quantity cannot be directly known, identify a correlated observable to stand in for it, recording the proxy's bias and validity conditions.

base.update_signal: the proxy's correlation to the target changes or breaks

included: selecting a correlated observable as a stand-in
recording proxy bias and validity conditions

pros.claim: A well-characterized proxy makes an otherwise inaccessible quantity partially knowable, with its bias stated so consumers can discount it
pros.example: using deployment frequency as a proxy for hard-to-measure team throughput

cons.claim: Proxies drift: a surrogate valid yesterday can decouple from the target and quietly mislead (Goodhart-style)
cons.example: a metric that becomes a target and stops tracking the thing it proxied

failure_modes: proxy treated as the target itself
proxy correlation assumed stable without re-check
acceptance_tests: each proxy records its target, its known bias, and the conditions under which it remains valid
revisit_triggers: the proxy-target correlation weakens
the proxy becomes an optimization target

nodes.definition: Actively search to convert unknown-unknowns into known-unknowns: deliberately seek disconfirming evidence, run premortems and red-teams, and probe outside the current frame to surface questions not yet asked.

base.update_signal: a probe surfaces a new question class or the frame is found too narrow

pros.claim: Active disconfirmation is the only operation that can move items out of the unknown-unknown cell, turning surprises into named gaps before they bite
pros.example: a premortem surfacing a failure mode the plan never considered

cons.claim: The search for unknown-unknowns is unbounded and can consume arbitrary effort with diminishing returns
cons.example: red-teaming a low-stakes decision until the budget is gone

failure_modes: confirmation bias makes the probe only seek supporting evidence
unbounded probing with no stopping rule
acceptance_tests: at least one disconfirmation-seeking probe is run with an explicit stopping rule proportional to stakes
revisit_triggers: a realized surprise reveals the frame was too narrow
stakes change enough to revisit probe depth

nodes.definition: Propagate uncertainty through inferences: combine the confidence states and assumptions feeding a conclusion so the conclusion inherits an honest, traceable uncertainty rather than a spuriously confident one.

base.update_signal: the inference chain or any input confidence state changes

included: combining input uncertainties into a conclusion
tracing which inputs dominate the result's uncertainty

pros.claim: Honest propagation prevents the laundering of uncertainty: a conclusion drawn from shaky inputs cannot present as more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
pros.example: a result inheriting the wide interval of the assumption it rests on

cons.claim: Naive independence assumptions in propagation can drastically understate combined uncertainty when inputs are correlated
cons.example: multiplying correlated errors as if independent

failure_modes: uncertainty laundered: conclusion firmer than its inputs
correlated inputs propagated as independent
acceptance_tests: each conclusion's stated uncertainty is no tighter than its dominant load-bearing input and shows that input
revisit_triggers: an input confidence state changes
a hidden correlation among inputs is discovered

nodes.definition: Maintain the living known/unknown map across the session: re-type items as evidence arrives, retire resolved gaps, register new ones, and keep the boundary, assumptions, and confidence states current and consistent.

base.update_signal: the map drifts from the current evidence or a re-typing is overdue

included: retiring resolved gaps and registering new ones

pros.claim: A maintained living map keeps the team's epistemic state honest over a session instead of decaying into a stale snapshot
pros.example: a resolved gap retired and its dependent conclusions upgraded the same session

cons.claim: Continuous re-typing has overhead and can churn: over-frequent updates destabilize the shared map
cons.example: re-scoring confidence on every minor signal until nothing settles

failure_modes: map decays into a stale snapshot
update churn destabilizes the shared epistemic state
acceptance_tests: the map reflects the latest evidence: resolved gaps retired, new gaps and re-typings applied, consistency preserved
revisit_triggers: new evidence arrives
a re-typing is overdue or the map contradicts itself

nodes.definition: Define the legality interface for downstream evidence use: rules stating which confidence labels and uncertainty types are permitted to support which downstream claims, so weakly-grounded knowns cannot be consumed as if certain.

base.update_signal: the downstream label-eligibility policy or evidence governance rules change

included: mapping confidence labels to permitted downstream uses

pros.claim: A legality interface is the gate that stops a speculative or assumption-grade claim from being consumed downstream as an experimentally-validated fact
pros.example: barring a 'heuristic' label from supporting a safety-critical decision

cons.claim: Over-strict legality rules can starve downstream reasoning of usable inputs, stalling decisions that could tolerate provisional evidence
cons.example: rejecting all provisional knowledge so no decision can proceed

failure_modes: weak claim consumed downstream as certain
legality so strict that usable provisional evidence is barred
acceptance_tests: each downstream use is checked against the legality of its inputs' confidence labels and uncertainty types
revisit_triggers: evidence governance policy changes
a weak claim is found to have been consumed as certain

edges.why_related: probing converts an unknown-unknown into a named known-unknown, feeding the gap pipeline
new evidence triggers re-typing of items on the living map
a proxy's known bias constrains the confidence state of any claim it supports
ambiguity must be dissolved by definition before an item counts as an empirical gap
deep uncertainty caps the value-of-information of acquisition since evidence may not reduce it
structural uncertainty widens the propagated uncertainty of any model-derived conclusion
resolved high-priority gaps are retired from the living map after acquisition

edges.resolution_rule: cap mapping effort at the point where the marginal gap's expected value-of-information falls below its identification cost; prioritize within the bounded set rather than seeking exhaustive enumeration
edges.why_related: exhaustive gap-mapping conflicts with the analysis cost of finding and typing every conceivable gap
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the epistemic map

edges.resolution_rule: treat uncertainty as epistemic (reducible by evidence) only while reduction efforts measurably move it; once they stall or parties cannot agree on a distribution, reclassify as deep and switch to robustness methods
edges.why_related: treating deep uncertainty as merely reducible-epistemic breeds overconfidence and false promises of reduction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the epistemic map

edges.resolution_rule: bound the search for unknown-unknowns with a stopping rule proportional to the decision's stakes; require each probe to be a structured premortem/red-team rather than open-ended speculation
edges.why_related: surfacing unknown-unknowns is valuable but the search is unbounded and can consume arbitrary effort
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the epistemic map

edges.resolution_rule: express confidence at the granularity calibration supports (intervals or ordinal bands, not invented decimals); legality gates on bands so coarse-but-honest states are usable while false-precise ones are rejected
edges.why_related: precise numeric confidence states risk false precision yet downstream legality wants discriminating labels
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the epistemic map

conflict_axes.name: exhaustive_gap_mapping_vs_analysis_cost
conflict_axes.description: Mapping every gap improves coverage but the search and typing cost is unbounded; stopping early risks missing a decision-relevant gap.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop when marginal gap VoI falls below identification cost; prioritize within the bounded set

conflict_axes.name: reducible_treatment_vs_honest_deep_uncertainty
conflict_axes.description: Treating uncertainty as reducible-epistemic enables action but, applied to deep uncertainty, manufactures overconfidence; honest deep-uncertainty handling forgoes tidy point estimates.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reclassify as deep once reduction stalls or distributions are contested; switch to robustness

conflict_axes.name: surface_unknown_unknowns_vs_unbounded_search
conflict_axes.description: Probing for unknown-unknowns reduces surprise risk but the search has no natural bound and can consume arbitrary effort.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stopping rule proportional to stakes; structured premortem/red-team over open speculation

conflict_axes.name: fine_grained_confidence_vs_false_precision
conflict_axes.description: Fine-grained confidence states discriminate claims usefully but invite fabricated precision beyond what calibration supports.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: express at the granularity calibration supports; gate legality on honest bands

conflict_axes.name: aleatory_vs_epistemic_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The split between irreducible and reducible uncertainty is model-relative; a hard label can either waste reduction effort or entrench avoidable ignorance.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record the system boundary under which a label holds; revisit when the model resolution changes

conflict_axes.name: surface_tacit_vs_over_formalization
conflict_axes.description: Eliciting unknown-knowns removes silent assumptions but over-formalizing tacit skill produces brittle false rules.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: elicit load-bearing tacit assumptions; test elicited rules against practice before relying on them

conflict_axes.name: frontier_clarity_vs_false_closure
conflict_axes.description: A crisp boundary artifact aligns the team but implies the far side is empty, encouraging the false-closure error.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always render an explicit residual-ignorance margin beyond the drawn frontier

conflict_axes.name: proxy_usefulness_vs_proxy_drift
conflict_axes.description: A proxy makes an inaccessible quantity partially knowable but can decouple from its target (Goodhart) and mislead.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record proxy bias and validity conditions; re-check correlation and watch for target-capture

conflict_axes.name: map_freshness_vs_update_churn
conflict_axes.description: Continuous re-typing keeps the map honest but over-frequent updates churn and destabilize the shared epistemic state.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-type on material evidence only; batch minor signals to avoid churn

edge_cases.description: An assumption is recorded but used downstream as if it were a justified known-known, so conclusions inherit false certainty.
edge_cases.trigger: a conditional known consumed without checking its confidence label
edge_cases.mitigation: legality interface bars assumption-grade labels from supporting certainty-grade claims

edge_cases.description: A genuinely deep uncertainty is forced into a single point estimate, producing overconfident planning.
edge_cases.mitigation: reclassify as deep when reduction stalls or distributions are contested; use robustness methods

edge_cases.description: The known/unknown map looks complete, so the team treats the recognized frontier as the whole territory and is blindsided by a surprise.
edge_cases.trigger: no residual-ignorance margin or active probe recorded
edge_cases.mitigation: always record a residual margin and run at least one disconfirmation probe

edge_cases.description: An item that is really an undefined term is routed to costly empirical acquisition instead of being defined.
edge_cases.trigger: ambiguity not screened before gap identification
edge_cases.mitigation: screen and dissolve ambiguity by definition before listing a gap as empirical

edge_cases.description: Effort is spent acquiring a low-impact unknown while a decision-flipping gap stays open.
edge_cases.trigger: gaps not ranked by value of information
edge_cases.mitigation: rank gaps by decision-impact against cost; address top-VoI gaps first

edge_cases.description: A proxy that once tracked its target decouples (Goodhart) and silently misleads downstream reasoning.
edge_cases.trigger: proxy correlation assumed stable; proxy becomes an optimization target
edge_cases.mitigation: record validity conditions; re-check correlation; flag target-capture

edge_cases.description: A conclusion is presented as firmer than its weakest load-bearing input because uncertainty was not propagated.
edge_cases.trigger: inference drawn without combining input confidence states
edge_cases.mitigation: propagate so a conclusion is no tighter than its dominant input; show that input

edge_cases.description: Correlated inputs are propagated as independent, drastically understating combined uncertainty.
edge_cases.mitigation: check for correlation among inputs before combining; widen the interval when found

edge_cases.description: Parameter intervals are tightened inside a structurally wrong model, giving false precision about the wrong thing.
edge_cases.trigger: measurement uncertainty reduced without validating model structure
edge_cases.mitigation: validate structure (rival models) before trusting tightened parameter intervals

edge_cases.description: Tacit knowledge stays unsurfaced and a silent assumption drives the analysis unchallenged.
edge_cases.mitigation: run elicitation on load-bearing items; register surfaced assumptions

edge_cases.description: The living map decays into a stale snapshot, so resolved gaps still show open and new evidence is ignored.
edge_cases.trigger: map not maintained as evidence arrives
edge_cases.mitigation: re-type on material evidence; retire resolved gaps; register new ones

edge_cases.description: A speculative claim is consumed downstream as an experimentally-validated fact because no legality gate exists.
edge_cases.trigger: downstream use not checked against input confidence labels
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the legality interface mapping labels to permitted downstream uses

workflow.description: For the question, separate justified known-knowns from everything else and record each known's justification.
workflow.gate: every known-known carries a justification and evidence reference

workflow.description: Name each recognized gap as an answerable question with an acquisition or estimation handle.
workflow.gate: each gap is phrased as an answerable question

workflow.description: Elicit unknown-knowns: surface tacit assumptions and institutional memory into explicit testable claims.
workflow.gate: material tacit assumptions are made explicit

workflow.description: Classify each uncertain item as aleatory, epistemic, ambiguity, model, measurement, or deep.
workflow.gate: each item has a nature tag with its reduction route

workflow.description: Screen for ambiguity and dissolve undefined terms by definition before any empirical acquisition is planned.
workflow.gate: no pseudo-gap (undefined term) remains on the empirical list

workflow.description: Record load-bearing assumptions as conditional knowns linked to the conclusions that depend on them.
workflow.gate: every load-bearing assumption is registered with its dependents

workflow.description: Attach a calibrated confidence state with an evidence label and interval to each claim.
workflow.gate: each claim carries a calibrated confidence state, not a bare point

workflow.description: Assign every item a complete type: knowledge cell, uncertainty nature, and recognition flag.
workflow.gate: every mapped item is fully typed

workflow.description: Enumerate decision-relevant gaps and rank them by value of information against acquisition cost.
workflow.gate: top gaps ranked by VoI with justification

workflow.description: Render the known/unknown frontier with populated cells, open gaps, and an explicit residual-ignorance margin.
Run a stakes-proportional premortem/red-team probe seeking disconfirming evidence and unasked questions.
workflow.gate: at least one bounded probe run with a stopping rule

workflow.description: Propagate uncertainty into conclusions and gate downstream use by confidence-label legality; then maintain the living map.
workflow.gate: no conclusion firmer than its inputs; downstream uses pass legality

dominance_rules.rule: AMBIGUITY_UNC must screen and dissolve undefined terms before GAP_IDENTIFY lists an item as an empirical gap
dominance_rules.rationale: an undefined term is dissolved by definition, not by costly acquisition
dominance_rules.trigger: a vague term is queued for empirical acquisition

dominance_rules.rule: DEEP_UNCERTAINTY must override EPISTEMIC treatment once reduction efforts stall or the distribution is contested
dominance_rules.rationale: treating deep uncertainty as reducible breeds overconfidence
dominance_rules.trigger: a reduction effort fails to move the uncertainty
dominance_rules.action: reclassify as deep and switch to robustness/scenario handling

dominance_rules.rule: CONFIDENCE_LEGALITY must gate any downstream use of a claim by the legality of its confidence label
dominance_rules.rationale: weak knowns consumed as certain corrupt downstream conclusions
dominance_rules.action: block uses whose inputs' labels are not legal for that use

dominance_rules.rule: UNC_PROPAGATION must run before a conclusion is published, and the conclusion's interval must be no tighter than its dominant input
dominance_rules.rationale: un-propagated uncertainty launders shaky inputs into firm-looking conclusions
dominance_rules.trigger: a conclusion is drawn from multiple uncertain inputs
dominance_rules.action: propagate and clamp the conclusion to its dominant input's uncertainty

dominance_rules.rule: BOUNDARY_OF_KNOWLEDGE must render an explicit residual-ignorance margin and at least one active probe before the map is treated as decision-ready
dominance_rules.rationale: a frontier with no margin invites the false-closure error
dominance_rules.trigger: the map is presented as complete
dominance_rules.action: require a residual margin and a DISCONFIRMATION probe

dominance_rules.rule: ASSUMPTION_REGISTRY must record every load-bearing assumption with its dependent conclusions before those conclusions are finalized
dominance_rules.rationale: unrecorded load-bearing assumptions make conclusions silently fragile
dominance_rules.trigger: a conclusion rests on an unverified proposition
dominance_rules.action: register the assumption and link its dependents

dominance_rules.rule: GAP_PRIORITIZE ranking by value of information governs which gaps GAP_IDENTIFY queues for acquisition
dominance_rules.rationale: acquisition effort is scarce and must buy decision-relevance
dominance_rules.trigger: acquisition is scheduled for a gap
dominance_rules.action: require the gap to clear a VoI-vs-cost threshold

dominance_rules.rule: PROXY_KNOWN may stand in for an inaccessible target only with its bias and validity conditions recorded
dominance_rules.rationale: an uncharacterized proxy silently misleads downstream consumers
dominance_rules.trigger: a proxy is used for a target quantity
dominance_rules.action: require recorded bias and validity conditions before consumption

dominance_rules.rule: IGNORANCE_TYPING must assign a complete type to every item before it is acted on
dominance_rules.rationale: untyped items get the wrong default treatment
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is queued for action without a type
dominance_rules.action: block action until cell, nature, and recognition are assigned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not consume an assumption as a justified known; verify or label it first, or all dependent conclusions need rework when it breaks
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding a conclusion chain after a silent assumption is invalidated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not list an undefined term as an empirical gap; define it first, or you research a pseudo-gap and re-scope later
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wasted acquisition on a question that was only an ambiguity

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not force deep uncertainty into a point estimate; switching to robustness after an overconfident plan fails is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replanning after an overconfident single-distribution bet fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat the recognized frontier as complete; discovering a missed question class late forces a full re-map
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-mapping after an unanticipated surprise

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not acquire low-VoI gaps before high-VoI ones; reordering after effort is spent wastes the acquisition budget
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redoing acquisition once a decision-flipping gap surfaces late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not publish a conclusion without propagating uncertainty; retrofitting honest intervals after the fact invalidates downstream use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalling conclusions consumed downstream as falsely certain

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not rely on a proxy without recording its bias and validity; untangling a drifted proxy's influence later is expensive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tracing and correcting decisions built on a decoupled proxy

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let the map go stale; reconciling a long-unmaintained map with reality costs more than incremental re-typing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a large reconciliation pass after the map diverges from evidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a realized surprise reveals a missed question class
iteration_protocol.action: run DISCONFIRMATION probes and re-bound UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN, then re-render the frontier in BOUNDARY_OF_KNOWLEDGE

iteration_protocol.trigger: an uncertainty reduction effort stalls without moving the estimate
iteration_protocol.action: reclassify the item from EPISTEMIC to DEEP_UNCERTAINTY and switch to robustness handling

iteration_protocol.trigger: a weak claim is found to have been consumed downstream as certain
iteration_protocol.action: tighten CONFIDENCE_LEGALITY rules and re-run UNC_PROPAGATION on affected conclusions
update ASSUMPTION_REGISTRY and re-type and re-confidence every dependent conclusion

iteration_protocol.trigger: an empirical gap turns out to be an undefined term
iteration_protocol.action: move it from GAP_IDENTIFY to AMBIGUITY_UNC and dissolve it by definition

iteration_protocol.trigger: a proxy decouples from its target
iteration_protocol.action: flag PROXY_KNOWN, discount the affected confidence states, and re-open the underlying gap

iteration_protocol.trigger: the decision or its payoffs change
iteration_protocol.action: re-run GAP_PRIORITIZE value-of-information ranking and reorder the acquisition queue

iteration_protocol.trigger: the living map drifts from current evidence
iteration_protocol.action: run MAP_MAINTENANCE to re-type items, retire resolved gaps, and restore consistency

priority_rationale: the four knowledge cells (KNOWN_KNOWN..UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN) are foundational; uncertainty-nature typing and the annotation layer (assumptions, confidence, ignorance typing) build on them; the gap pipeline (identify, prioritize, frontier, proxy) and active epistemics (disconfirmation, propagation, maintenance, legality) close the method.
